Here is my translation of this passage from Homer's *Iliad* (Book 19, lines 184-197):

Then in turn the lord of men Agamemnon addressed him:
"I rejoice, son of Laertes, to hear your speech;
for you have gone through all things properly and recounted them in due measure.
These things I am willing to swear, and my heart bids me to do so,
nor shall I swear falsely before the god. But let Achilles
remain here for a time, though he is eager for war;
and do all the rest of you remain gathered together, until the gifts
come from my hut and we cut trustworthy oaths.
To you yourself I give this charge and command:
selecting the best young men of all the Achaeans,
bring the gifts from my ship, all those which
yesterday we promised to give to Achilles, and bring the women too.
And let Talthybius quickly throughout the broad army of the Achaeans
prepare a boar to sacrifice to Zeus and to Helios."

**Context:** This is Agamemnon responding to Odysseus during the reconciliation scene with Achilles. Agamemnon agrees to make a formal oath and present the compensation gifts he had promised to Achilles for taking Briseis.
